1. INDUSTRY STRUCTURE AND DEVELOPMENT
The aerospace and defence sector is undergoing a
significant structural shift driven by evolving geopolitical
dynamics, rapid technological advancements and
increasing emphasis on self-reliance, witnessed sustained
momentum during FY 2025-26, supported by the
Government’s continued focus on “Atmanirbhar Bharat”,
indigenisation, and modernisation of the Armed Forces.
Geopolitical uncertainties and the need to enhance
operational readiness drove higher demand for indigenous
platforms, including fighter aircraft, helicopters, engines,
and related systems.
Key structural shifts included greater private sector
participation in the defence ecosystem, policy support
through positive indigenisation lists, export promotion
measures, and infrastructure development for aerospace
manufacturing. The sector is transitioning towards
higher self-reliance, with increased emphasis on design,
development, and production of advanced platforms such
as the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas, Advanced Light
Helicopter (ALH) Dhruv variants, Light Combat Helicopter
(LCH) Prachand, and trainer aircraft.
HAL as India’s leading aerospace and defence Maharatna
PSU, maintains its pivotal role in design, development,
Manufacturing, Repair, Overhaul (MRO), and upgrade of
a wide range of aircraft, helicopters, engines, and avionics
systems. The Company has contributed significantly to
fleet availability and indigenisation efforts, while the
industry as a whole saw record-level order inflows and
production ramp-ups in select segments.
2. ORGANISATION STRUCTURE
Presently, the Company has 20 Divisions and 10 R&D
Centres. These Divisions and R&D Centres are located
at ten geographic locations in seven states across the
Country. HAL’s Divisions and R&D Centres are organized
into five Complexes with current & future operations
given below:
 Bangalore Complex (BC): Production, MRO and
upgrade of Fixed-wing Aircraft and Engines of Indian
and Western origin, Aerospace Structures & Castings,
Forgings & Rolled Rings.
 MiG Complex (MC): Production of indigenous Fixed
wing aircraft, Production, MRO and upgrade of Fixed-
wing aircraft and Engines of mainly Russian origin,
Civil MRO and UAV Projects.
 Helicopter Complex (HC): Production, MRO and
upgrade of Helicopters of Indian and Western origin.
Production of Composite parts for Fixed and Rotary
wing platforms.
 Accessories Complex (AC): Production, MRO and
upgrade of Transport Aircraft. Production and MRO
of Accessories and Avionics for Fixed-wing and
Rotary-wing Platforms (Indian, Russian and Western
origin). Depot Level Maintenance of UAVs.
 Design Complex (DC): R&D of Fixed-wing and Rotary-
wing aircraft, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV), Aero-
engines, Avionics and Accessories.
BC, MC, HC and AC are headed by Chief Executive Officers
(CEOs). Head of Divisions under each Complex reports to
the respective CEOs, whereas Head of R&D Centres under
Design Complex report to Director (Engineering and R&D).
All the Functional Directors and CEOs report to Chairman
& Managing Director (CMD).
3. SWOT ANALYSIS
SWOT Analysis is the tool to identify potential opportunities
and threats in the external environment and assess internal
strengths and weaknesses of the organization. The SWOT
analysis of the Company is as follows:
Strengths
 Integrated aerospace business which includes R&D,
Production and MRO including PBL solutions of
the Fixed-wing aircraft, Rotary-wing aircraft, Aero-
engines, LRUs and airborne systems.
 Strong order book ensuring long-term revenue
visibility.
 Expertise in aircraft upgrade for the Defence
Customers which includes major changes like re-
engining, avionics upgrade, and weapon system
integration.
 Expertise in execution of Transfer of Technology (ToT)
projects. The Company has successfully absorbed ToT
and produced MiG-21, MiG-27, Su-30MKI, Jaguar,
Hawk, Dornier-228 and AVRO.
 Expertise in Design & Development of a wide range of
helicopters including Utility and Combat helicopters.
The Company has developed flagship platforms
like ALH Variants, LCH, LUH in 3.5-to-5.5-ton class.
Also, the Company has foray into Civil Helicopter by
developing ALH Dhruv-NG (Next Generation). Further,

15-ton class, proving D&D capabilities in wide range
of helicopters.
 Trusted partner of Indian Defence Forces for providing
support to aging fleets, some of which are more than
60 years old.
Weaknesses
 Dependency on foreign OEMs for critical materials
and LRUs.
 Long gestation periods and complexities in project
execution.
 Limited presence in high-value global export markets.
Opportunities
 Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan and other policy
reforms such as Positive Indigenisation List (PIL) by the
Government promoting self-reliance and indigenous
products.
 Focus of Government to develop A&D ecosystem
in the Country to reduce import bill and make India
A&D hub.
 Civil MRO opportunities in India, expansion in MRO
and lifecycle support services.
 Development of new potential market in India such
as for regional jets, UAVs etc.
Threats
 Collaborations of Indian Private Companies with
Global OEMs and capability building by their entities.
 Change in preference of regular customers by moving
from nomination to competitive procurement.
 Rapid technological disruptions requiring continuous
upgradation.
 Direct competition from foreign companies
entering into Indian market and pricing pressures in
international markets.
 Mainly dependent on MoD for the contracts. Any
change in procurement policy / preference can
adversely affect our ability to grow or maintain our
sales, earnings and cash flow.
 Supply chain disruptions due to geopolitical issues.
4. OUR STRATEGIES
We intend to pursue the following principal strategies to
leverage our strengths and grow our business:
 Enhance Indigenisation content in our products.
 Enhance export sales.
 Expanding production capabilities to meet growing
demand.
 Enhance customer satisfaction and improved quality
of products and services.
 Investing in R&D and adopting advanced
manufacturing technologies.
 Opening Export Offices in the target geographies to
explore global market and export opportunities.
 Progress Design and Development programs with
initial company funding for Indian Defence Services.
 Focus on increasing operational efficiencies by
adapting technologies such as Industry 4.0,
automation, additive manufacturing, etc.

The Ministry of Corporate Affairs vide Notification No.
1/2/2014-CL-V dated February 23, 2018 has exempted

to the extent of application of Ind AS 108 on “Operating

6. OUTLOOK
The outlook for FY 2026-27 and beyond will remain
positive, supported by a strong order book providing 7-8
years of revenue visibility. The Company expects improved
growth through better supply chain stabilization, capacity
expansion (including significant infrastructure investments)
and faster production ramp-up for key platforms.
Focus areas include:
- Achieving higher production rates for LCA Mk1A
(targeting 24+ aircraft annually in coming years).
- Expediting the production rate of HTT-40.
- Expanding civil and export segments.
- Enhancing indigenisation levels (aiming 65-75%+ for
major platforms).
89

- Digital transformation, AI integration, and R&D for
future programs like IMRH, LCA Mk2, CATS, HLFT
and UAVs.
The Company is well-positioned to capitalize on these
opportunities, across aircraft, helicopters, aero engines,
avionics, and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO)
projects. Execution of ongoing programmes, coupled with
anticipated new orders in fighter aircraft, rotary-wing
platforms, and upgrade projects, is expected to provide
revenue visibility over the medium to long term.
In parallel, the Company is intensifying efforts to expand
its global footprint through exports and strategic
collaborations with international partners. Emerging
opportunities in areas such as unmanned systems,
advanced materials, digital manufacturing, and space
applications are expected to open new growth avenues.
However, the outlook is subject to certain challenges,
which includes, evolving technological requirements,
supply chain constraints and increasing competition both
from private sector and global players. The Company’s
focus on enhancing operational efficiency, strengthening
its supply chain ecosystem, accelerating indigenisation,
and investing in research and development is expected to
mitigate these risks.
The Company is poised to sustain its growth trajectory and
reinforce its position as a key enabler of India’s aerospace
and defence capabilities while progressively enhancing its
competitiveness in the global market.
7. RISKS AND CONCERNS
The major risks and concerns for the Company are:
 Dependence on foreign OEMs for supply of critical
components and Spares.
 Dependence on limited customers for new contracts.
 Competition from domestic and foreign players.
 Rapid advancements leading to obsolescence of
existing systems.
 Challenges in meeting aggressive timelines for
complex indigenous platforms, integration issues,
and certification requirements.
8. MEASURES TO TACKLE CHALLENGES, CONCERNS
AND RISKS
The Company has identified the following focus areas to
address the challenges, concerns and risks:
 Indigenisation and Technology Initiatives: Accelerated
R&D, partnerships for technology transfer (e.g., higher
localization in engines), and vendor development
programs to reduce import dependence.
 Diversification of suppliers, development of alternate
indigenous sources, and closer coordination with
global suppliers (including resolution of engine supply
issues observed in prior periods). Building strategic
inventories for critical items.
 Capacity and Infrastructure Build-up: Significant
CAPEX investments in new production facilities,
modernization of existing lines and establishment of
additional assembly lines to de-risk execution.
 Dedicated marketing efforts and government-
supported export initiatives.
 Market-oriented products and technology
developments to complement with company goals to
expand in commercial and export market.
 Enhanced digitalization and IT & AI enabled systems
for speedy communication and decision-making.
 Use of advanced materials, Advanced Manufacturing
Technologies and automation to improve product
quality and achieve operational efficiencies.
9. CUSTOMER ORIENTATION
The Company is committed for providing timely support to
its customers. Also, focussing on continuous improvements
and responsiveness to the needs of Customers. Achieving
Customer satisfaction is not merely a goal for us but a
core responsibility. The Company continues to devise
innovative solutions and ensure effective implementation
towards achieving total customer satisfaction.
During the year, the Company has undertaken following
initiatives towards customer orientation:
i. Indian Army-HAL Vayu (Virtual Automation
Yielding Unification) Portal - The Portal has been
officially launched for integration of Army and HAL
ERP databases towards ensuring transparent & real-
time aviation logistic supply chain.
ii. Digitisation of Supply Chain - Actions have been
initiated for full scale digitization of supply chain.
Quality certification digitized in Helicopter, Overhaul,
Aircraft & LCA Divisions.
iii. Dedicated RMSO Management Team at
Divisional Level - Dedicated RMSO Management
Team are set up at all Divisions towards ensuring
serviceability of HAL Platforms and spares supply.
